clue.text: Parts of male formal wear reordered as female wear?

indicators.note: to reorder is to put in a different sequence, so the order changes

blocks.note: a dress shirt is the stiff white shirt worn with a dinner jacket; its two words are the parts

explanation.surface: A man's evening outfit is rearranged into something for a woman to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the two words of DRESS SHIRT and you have SHIRT DRESS; only the word order changes, not the letters within each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirtdress is a woman's dress cut like a long buttoned shirt, so it is clothing for women.

clue.text: Hearts not in surprise hit

indicators.note: 'not in' says something is absent from what follows, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
a shock is a sudden surprise

explanation.surface: A romance that leaves feelings out of it unexpectedly becomes a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H out of SHOCK to leave SOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is informal slang for punching or striking them hard.

clue.text: Restless troublemaker game to stop soldier

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
a soldier ant is a fighting caste of ant, so soldier often gives ANT
a tie is a single match in a knockout competition, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A fidgety troublemaker invents a game to keep a soldier from going anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' gives an insect, the fighting soldier ant. A cup tie is a British term for one knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless cannot wait calmly, which is exactly what being impatient means.

clue.text: Arranged research into origin of pole dancing

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
the origin of something is where it starts, so take its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the opening letter of pole

explanation.surface: Someone has organised academic study into how pole dancing began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to shuffle. Terpsichore is the Greek Muse of dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichorean is a formal adjective meaning relating to the art of dance, named after the Muse of that art.

clue.text: Memory linked to personal baby wear

blocks.note: ROM is read-only memory in a computer
PERS is a standard abbreviation for personal

explanation.surface: A sentimental keepsake tied to an infant's own clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: ROM is the computing abbreviation for read-only memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Rompers are one-piece play suits worn by infants and toddlers, so they are clothing for little children.

clue.text: A Parisian getting thump in pursuit of shilling or tanner

indicators.note: to be in pursuit is to come behind, so this part is placed after another

blocks.note: s was the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money
un is French for 'a'
to lamp someone is British slang for hitting them

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is punched while chasing old British coins, a shilling or a sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was an old British sixpence, so 'shilling or tanner' reads as coins; here the tanner is anything that tans you. The shilling was a pre-1971 coin worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp gives off ultraviolet light that darkens skin, so it is a device that tans people.

clue.text: End for Achilles and Hector in a boat?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of Achilles
to hector is to bully, and to cow is to intimidate

explanation.surface: Two Trojan War heroes, Achilles and Hector, meet their end together on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector is capitalised to look like the Trojan prince, but it is the verb meaning to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed barge used for carrying cargo, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Pink colour’s beginning around the mouth

indicators.note: a beginning is where something starts, so take the opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of colour
oral means relating to the mouth

explanation.surface: A pink tint first appears around someone's lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink colour' looks like one phrase, but only 'Pink' defines; 'colour's beginning' supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange shade named after the sea creature's skeleton, so it is a hue of pink.

clue.text: Questions that chap about energy and fertiliser primarily delivering farm product

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another
primarily means first of all, so only the initial letters are kept

blocks.note: 'What's he?' is how you would question a man
E is the symbol for energy
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone quizzes a farmer about his power and fertiliser use as he produces crops.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside WHAT'S HE, then AF is added; 'primarily' applies to both 'and' and 'fertiliser'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheatsheaf is a bundle of harvested wheat stalks tied together, an output of arable farming.

clue.text: King welcomes parody crime

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece is received inside another

blocks.note: CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
to ape is to mimic or parody

explanation.surface: A monarch delights in a satirical take on a criminal act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parody' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in to mimic someone. The royal cipher of King Charles is Carolus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is an informal word for a daring illegal escapade such as a robbery.

clue.text: Chaps get on and ride, abandoning 500 animals

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: chaps are men
to get on is to grow older
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Riders mount up and leave behind a herd of five hundred beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' suggests mounting a horse, but it means growing old. RIDE loses D to give RIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition, so the word stands for a group of creatures.

clue.text: Climate impact: large drop concerning around start of winter

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps round another
the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: a glob is a large blob or drop of liquid
concerning means worrying
the opening letter of winter

explanation.surface: A climate report notes a big fall in temperature that worries scientists as winter begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' looks like 'about', but it is the adjective meaning worrying; W goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Global warming is the rise in Earth's average temperature, a principal effect of climate change.

clue.text: Succeeded occupying area returned to original state, reflecting part of bigger picture

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside, so one letter goes within another piece
a reflection is a mirror image, so everything is read backwards

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
to reset is to put back to the starting condition
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A conquered region goes back to how it was, mirroring the larger historical picture.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes into RESET, A comes in front, and the whole lot is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles that make up a mosaic, a fragment of the whole image.

clue.text: Couple rejected pinioning wings of large baby bird

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so this piece is turned around
wings are on either side, so the two outside letters are kept
to pinion is to pin someone's arms, holding them fast inside

blocks.note: a couple is two
the outside letters of large

explanation.surface: A pair of people refuse to help, clipping the wings of a big young bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinioning wings fits the bird surface while doing a different job: the wings are just the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, a chick of that species.

clue.text: Unsuitable male sadly hugging rugby player with love (10)|

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap your arms round, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
alas is an exclamation of sorrow
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An unfit man sadly embraces a rugby player he loves.
explanation.walkthrough: ALAS holds PROP and O. In rugby, the props are the two front-row forwards who bind in the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Malapropos is a formal adjective for something inappropriate or ill-timed, the opposite of apropos.

clue.text: Insights originally captured in a study left unfinished

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the opening letter is taken
something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter goes
to be in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
to peruse is to read or study carefully
the opening letter of captured

explanation.surface: Fresh insights came from an unfinished piece of research.
explanation.walkthrough: PERUSE loses its E to become PERUS, and C goes inside that, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief revealing glimpse or remark, borrowed from French, so these are flashes of understanding.

clue.text: Old King of advanced age back beside pub

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run backwards
beside means next to, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: PH is a public house on a map
A stands for advanced, as in A level
hoar is an old, poetic noun for the greyness of age

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch, getting on in years, sits next to the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced age' reads as one phrase but splits into A and HOAR; only HOAR is reversed. A level is the British school-leaving exam, short for Advanced level.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a ruler of ancient Egypt, a monarch from antiquity.

clue.text: Cool way to get in a revolutionary quote

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so these letters are turned around
getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to cite is to quote
a path is a way

explanation.surface: A trendy route into a radical slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' suggests trendy but means unenthusiastic, and 'revolutionary' applies only to the quote.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cool towards something means showing little interest or enthusiasm, which is what apathetic describes.

clue.text: Biblical city opposing comment of St Andrews?

blocks.note: anti means against
och is a Scottish exclamation, and St Andrews is in Scotland

explanation.surface: A town in the Bible stands against something said in a Scottish university town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews is a Scottish town, home of golf; the question mark flags that it stands for any Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was an ancient Syrian city where, according to Acts, followers of Jesus were first called Christians.

clue.text: Harry – name needed – in irons, initially!

definitions.text: Harry – name needed – in irons, initially!

indicators.note: something needed is lacking, so a letter is missing
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to harry and to hound both mean to pursue relentlessly
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written
the opening letter of irons

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry, whose surname we want, is first seen chained up.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUND without N gives HOUD, then IN and I. Read whole, the clue describes the escapologist Harry Houdini, famous for escaping chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the celebrated escape artist who freed himself from handcuffs, chains and shackles on stage.

clue.text: An ace internet publication mostly about NZ material

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I
a wiki is a collaboratively edited website

explanation.surface: A first-rate website is mainly about New Zealand stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: AN, AI and WIK (WIKI cut short) are reversed together. A Kiwi is a New Zealander.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwiana are objects and icons seen as typical of New Zealand culture, such as pavlova and jandals.

clue.text: Sudden effort to follow castle’s exercise regime

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
a fit is a sudden burst of activity

explanation.surface: A burst of activity follows a castle's workout routine.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEP comes first because the burst 'follows' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep-fit is a British term for regular physical exercise classes done to stay healthy.

clue.text: Weapon student buried in common

indicators.note: something buried is put inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: rife means widespread
L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A gun belonging to a student lies buried on the village common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' looks like a stretch of public land but is the adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, one example of an armament.

clue.text: Mark‘s heading for front row

indicators.note: a heading is at the top, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of front
a rank is a row of soldiers

explanation.surface: Mark is making for the front row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, which suits the other man's name in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To frank a letter is to stamp it with a postal mark showing postage is paid.

clue.text: Discover some of you near Thetford

indicators.note: some of means a part only, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: Find out what lies near Thetford, a market town in Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'you' into the start of 'Thetford'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or bring it to light, which is finding it.

clue.text: Disparaging comment on Parisian cuddling student

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: sur is French for on
L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A snide remark about a Frenchman getting close to a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on Parisian' means the French word for on.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insinuation or insult that damages someone's reputation.

clue.text: Spat behind unattractive person in suit

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: plain means not good-looking
a spat and a tiff are both petty quarrels

explanation.surface: A row breaks out behind an ugly man wearing a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a lawsuit against another in a civil court.

clue.text: Information in unconscious body language? Not all of it

indicators.note: not all means part is missing, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
in poker a tell is an involuntary gesture that gives your hand away

explanation.surface: What can be learned from someone's involuntary gestures, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but supplies two letters; TELL loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Intel is informal shorthand for intelligence, meaning gathered facts about an enemy or rival.

clue.text: British writer spoke mostly about King

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: said is the past tense of say
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An English author talked mainly about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: SAID cut short is SAI, which goes round K. Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki was an Edwardian British author famous for witty, macabre short stories.

clue.text: New Testament period adopted by member of clergy, no modern saloon here

indicators.note: to be adopted is to be taken in, so these pieces go inside another

blocks.note: NT is the standard abbreviation
an age is a period of time
a vicar is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar takes up Bible study, though nothing like a modern bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is the British word for a sedan car, not a bar, so the definition rules out a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage car is an old automobile, typically built in the 1920s, so it is far from a contemporary model.
